scoring._README: score = sum of the components below. Higher = more brief-worthy. Candidates are pre-sorted by score desc; each item's `score_breakdown` shows its parts.
scoring.recency: 0–1h = 2.3 (breaking) · 1–3h = 2.0 (fresh) · then linear decay to 0 by 24h · unknown = 0.5
scoring.signal: AI/tech (or watchlist) keyword hits — match_count capped at 5 × 0.6
scoring.source: outlet authority from trusted-sources.md: primary (company/lab) 2.0 · citation 1.2 · screening 0.5 · other 1.0
scoring.corrob: cross-outlet corroboration — how many outlets ran the same headline (cluster_size − 1, capped 3) × 0.8
scoring.watchlist: watchlist stream only: matched company tier — Tier-1 +1.5 · Tier-2 +0.8

candidates.body_text: Oracle News Press Release NetApp and Oracle to Launch Fully Managed Cloud Storage Service for Demanding AI and Enterprise Workloads Secure, reliable, and performant NetApp storage is planned to be available as a native service to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure customers San Jose, California and Austin, Texas—Sep 29, 2026 NetApp® (NASDAQ: NTAP), the Intelligent Data Infrastructure company, and Oracle today announced a new fully managed storage service that brings enterprise-grade NetApp storage natively to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). The service will bring NetApp ONTAP® data management capabilities natively to OCI to help organizations simplify the migration and management of critical AI and enterprise workloads in the cloud. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure NetApp Storage Service is designed to be a fully managed OCI-native storage service that brings NetApp ONTAP data management capabilities to OCI. candidates.title: Meta is expanding its AI agent Muse to small businesses
candidates.description: Meta is expanding its AI agent Muse to small businesses    TechCrunch
candidates.body_text: Meta announced on Tuesday that it’s expanding its AI agent Muse to small businesses and adding new integrations, including Shopify, Dropbox, Slack, and more. The tech giant says the agent can help owners run their business and find new customers. By plugging Muse into the software that small business owners are already using to manage sales, operations, and marketing, Meta is betting that an AI agent with context of a company’s whole operation will be more useful than a stand-alone chatbot, as it continues to compete against rivals like OpenAI and Google. Muse can also link to Instagram professional account analytics, Facebook pages, and Meta ad accounts. Meta says the AI agent also knows what a business sells, how a brand sounds, and what customers ask about most. Additional integrations include Asana, Box, Canva, Figma, Granola, HighLevel, Intuit QuickBooks, Klaviyo, Lovable, Notion, Stripe, and Zoom. Muse for Small Business is available for free with usage limits. Businesses that want more usage can purchase a subscription plan. IMAGE CREDITS:META “Small businesses have been growing on our apps for nearly two decades,” Meta wrote in their blog post. “They told us they’re short on hours, not ideas. So we built Muse for Small Business to help get work done with the tools they already use.” Meta has been focused on expanding its AI tools beyond the consumer and into the enterprise market. candidates.description: Dan Niles predicts Microsoft, Apple and Google will dominate AI market    Fox Business
candidates.body_text: On Air September 29, 2026 01:49 CLIP Dan Niles predicts Microsoft, Apple and Google will dominate AI market Niles Investment Management founder Dan Niles predicts that Microsoft, Apple and Google will ultimately dominate the competitive artificial intelligence market. He outlines how these major tech giants will win. Microsoft, Apple and Google are positioned to dominate the artificial intelligence landscape as the industry transitions into a winner-take-most market. Niles Investment Management founder Dan Niles explains why Microsoft will capture the enterprise sector, while Apple and Google will split consumer ecosystems on mobile devices. He warns that smaller AI startups face massive challenges competing against these tech giants. candidates.body_text: SHARE Artificial Intelligence Corporate Data Center Media Alert: AMD CEO Lisa Su to Lead Keynote at 2026 OCP The leader of AMD will highlight how the company delivers the open, full-stack infrastructure required for agentic AI. PUBLISHED September 29, 2026 Dr. Lisa Su, chair and CEO at AMD, will deliver an opening keynote at the 2026 OCP Global Summit on Oct. 12, 2026. (Credit: AMD) Dr. Lisa Su, chair and CEO at AMD, will deliver an opening keynote at the 2026 OCP Global Summit on Oct. 12, 2026. As the open computing ecosystem gathers, Su will highlight the portfolio of open, full-stack infrastructure for agentic AI that AMD delivers at every scale – from enterprise systems to gigawatt-scale deployments. What: The four-day Open Compute Project Global Summit offers industry leaders a chance to explore advances in open infrastructure for artificial intelligence and data centers. Keynote: 4:15 p.m. PDT, Monday, Oct. 12 Where and When: San Jose McEnery Convention Center, 150 W. San Carlos St., San Jose, California; the event runs Oct. 12-15 AMD and Its Role: AMD delivers the industry’s most powerful and flexible agentic AI infrastructure across a broad portfolio of systems powered by leadership compute.​ Throughout the event, AMD and its partners will showcase platforms, demos and customer use cases.
